title: Harden reusable async scoring queue and log lifecycle
description: Add executable infrastructure specifications, implement retry-safe visibility validation, explicit log retention, and retained queue lifecycle defaults in the reusable async score processing construct. Keep downstream deployment details outside Plexus.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Started implementation. Verified live consumers currently synthesize a 300-second queue visibility timeout for a 300-second Lambda timeout and rely on an implicit log group. Plan: add failing CDK specifications, enforce the six-times visibility invariant, define an explicit retained log group, retain construct-owned queues, and validate that no downstream identifiers enter Plexus.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Implementation complete on the feature branch. Added the six-times visibility invariant, 1,800-second safe default, retained construct-owned queues, an explicit 30-day retained log group in a collision-free namespace, scoped log permissions, documentation, and executable CDK assertions. Validation: python -m pytest infrastructure/tests/unit infrastructure/score_processor_artifacts/tests/unit -q (15 passed); black --check on changed Python files; ruff check on changed Python files.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Opened PR #519 to develop. GitHub Actions did not start any jobs because the organization account reports failed payments or an exhausted spending limit; this is an external CI billing blocker, not a test failure. Local project validation remains green, and the task stays in progress until CI can run and the PR lands.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Live ECR validation of the new production artifact found 4 critical and 26 high OS-package findings. Root cause is the scoring Dockerfile installing git, Graphviz, libcurl, and libpq despite the scoring runtime using copied source and binary Python wheels. Security remediation is being tracked separately under the artifact epic; no production consumer will be deployed with this digest.

comments.author: unknown
comments.text: Board audit 2026-10-17: verified against develop. Merged via PR #519: primus/infrastructure/constructs/async_score_processing.py enforces the 6x visibility invariant with an 1800s default, retains construct-owned queues, and creates an explicit 30-day retained log group. Covered by infrastructure/tests/unit/test_async_score_processing_construct.py and documented in infrastructure/docs/async-score-processing-construct.md.
